page: Amazon Web Services c6gd.2xlarge is an ARM64-based compute-optimized server powered by an 8-core AWS Graviton2 processor using the Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture. Running on the Nitro hypervisor, it features 8 dedicated physical cores with single-thread-per-core execution at 2.5 GHz. The CPU is equipped with 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core allocation, and is bundled with 474 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across several multi-core and memory-bound workloads. The instance achieves a stress-ng multi-core score of 12133.14 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5364.0. Memory bandwidth is notable, reaching 473.11 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 116.89 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, with a Geekbench single-core score of 930.0 and a poor single-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 6.93 GB/sec. Cryptographic performance is also limited, as shown by a low PassMark CPU encryption score of 1084.81, despite hardware AES support.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c6gd.2xlarge offers a balanced compute-to-storage profile by combining dedicated ARM cores with high-speed local NVMe storage, avoiding the overhead of network-attached storage for temporary data. This makes it highly suitable for workloads that benefit from local scratch space and multi-core scaling, such as software compilation, static web serving, database operations, and redis caching. It is less suited for single-threaded tasks, heavy cryptographic operations, or large language model inference.
description: Amazon Web Services c6gd.2xlarge is an ARM64 compute-optimized server featuring 8 dedicated physical cores powered by an AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, 474 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, the instance delivers average multi-core and memory-bandwidth performance, as demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 12133.14 and a cached read bandwidth of 473.11 GB/sec. However, single-core and cryptographic performance are relatively weak, with a Geekbench single-core score of 930.0. This server is qualitatively cost-efficient for multi-threaded workloads requiring fast local scratch storage, making it well-suited for software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and caching, while being less optimal for single-threaded or heavy cryptographic tasks.
